journal:
# Reem (p10) — BodyTracker journal

## Day 1 (Sun 2026-10-04)
- Setup was clear. 158 cm, 33, 70.2 kg, female formula, "Lightly active", eating the same 2+ weeks = Yes, update day Sunday.
- My profile weight got saved as today's weigh-in automatically — nice, I didn't have to enter it twice.
- Popup: "Safari can clear data for sites you haven't opened in 7 days. Add to Home Screen." Hmm, that worries me a bit — what if I don't open it for a week? (I can't add to home screen from here.)
- After setup the target said "maintain" — I had to find the ⚙ on the Nutrition tab to pick "Lose". Would have liked the goal question in the setup itself. Default 0.5%/week, I kept it.
- Numbers: maintenance 1,870 ± 440 (Estimated, 0% from your data), target 1,510 kcal for lose 0.5%/wk. Protein 126 g.
- Logged 4 meals = 1,775 kcal (already 265 over target on day 1, pizza...). Ticked "Day complete" — the checkbox is above the "Add entry" form so I almost missed it.
- The "Water events" tags (High salt, Menstrual cycle, Illness, Travel...) are interesting — I'll remember "Illness".

## Day 2 (Mon)
- Wanted to enter my weight; tapped the big "Weight" on the Body tab and got a chart instead. The add form is the small "+ Weight" button. Minor, but I tapped the wrong thing first.
- Weight form: date/time pre-filled, nice. 70.2 again.
- Logged 4 meals, 1,576 kcal, marked complete. Still ~65 over 1,510.
- Recommendation box still says "needs 14 days of data (day 1 so far)" on day 2 — I guess it only refreshes on Sundays, but "day 1 so far" reads like it didn't count today.
- New note: "Protein averaged 100 g on 2 logged days vs 126 g target." Useful.

## Day 3 (Tue)
- Scale 69.9. Body tab shows "▼ 0.3 kg" but "Trend weight 70.2 kg" — took me a second: the trend is a smoothed line, so it barely moves. OK.
- 1,630 kcal logged, complete. Average so far 1,660 — I keep going over the 1,510 target by ~150. Not changing yet, waiting for the weekly update.

## Day 4 (Wed)
- 69.1 kg! "▼ 1.1 kg" vs first. Found the "vs First / vs Last" switch at the top — "vs Last" shows ▼0.8 since yesterday. Handy.
- 1,486 kcal — first day under target. Complete.

## Day 5 (Thu)
- Scale jumped back up to 69.8 (from 69.1). The ▼ went from 1.1 to 0.4. A bit discouraging, but trend says 70.0, steady down.
- 1,386 kcal, complete. Average 1,571.
- Opened "Explain the math →". Way too much math for me (Kalman filter, Hall 2008, Forbes...), but one sentence stuck: unlogged days are treated as "unknown, not zero" and the app assumes my usual average. Good to know.
- It says the numbers shown are "from the weekly update on 2026-10-04 (day 1)" — that explains the "day 1 so far".

## Day 6 (Fri)
- 68.6 kg on the scale — lowest yet. 1,252 kcal logged (lighter day), complete.
- Routine feels quick now: weigh, 4 meals, tick complete.

## Day 7 (Sat)
- 69.1. 1,419 kcal, complete. A full week logged, every day complete.

## Week 1 (update Sun 2026-10-11, day 8)
- App said: maintenance 1,970 ± 430 kcal/day, "Estimated", 4% from my data. Target 1,620 (lose 0.5%/wk). Avg intake 1,458, weight trend −0.46 kg/week (range −0.89 to −0.04). Protein 92 g vs 125 g target. On-track check needs 14 days.
- Warnings: "2026-10-09: macros add up to ~1051 kcal vs 1252 logged (16% apart)" and same for 10-10 (20%). I just copied what my calorie app/labels said... I don't know which one is wrong. Not going to go back and fix.
- Body composition: "Not enough data yet" (no body fat).
- What I understand: my body burns ~1,970, I'm eating ~1,460 and losing a bit faster than the goal. The app is basically telling me I can eat a little more (1,620).
- Decision: follow it — plan 1,620 kcal/day. Also try more protein (I'm at 92 g, it wants 125).
- Weekly update day being Sunday works, I saw the numbers change today (was 1,870 / 1,510).

## Days 9–14 (scripted routine, run.mjs)
- Same routine every day: weigh at 06:50, 4 meals, tick complete. My script stopped twice because of meals where I only knew calories (+protein) — I just typed calories and left macros empty. The app accepted that fine.
- Scale went 68.0 → 68.5 → 68.7 → 68.5 → 68.6 → 69.3. Annoying — eating ~1,620 as the app suggested and the scale went UP. Trend still slowly down though.
- Nothing new popped up during the week; the recommendation box stays frozen until Sunday (which I now understand).

## Week 2 (update Sun 2026-10-18, day 15)
- Scale 69.9 today (ugh). Trend 69.3.
- App: "On track. Your estimated rate (−0.73 to +0.02 kg/week) includes your target of −0.35 kg/week. Suggested intake 1,570 kcal/day."
- Maintenance 1,920 ± 390, Estimated, 22% from my data. Avg intake 1,632, rate −0.35 kg/wk (14-day). 7/7 days complete. Protein 85 g vs 125 g (still low!).
- My take: "on track" is reassuring even though the scale scared me this morning. The range going up to +0.02 kg/week means it's not even sure I'm losing though.
- Decision: plan 1,570 (slightly less than I've been eating). Need more protein — maybe more eggs/chicken.

## Days 16–22 (script)
- Scale bounced 69.8, 69.4, 69.7, 69.5, 69.9, 68.5, 69.0. Eating ~1,580–1,730. Feels like I'm stuck around 69–70.
- Nothing popped up mid-week. (Oops: my script ran right through Sunday, so I read the week-3 update Monday morning instead.)

## Week 3 (update Sun 2026-10-25, day 22; read Mon morning)
- "On track. Your estimated rate (−0.55 to +0.08 kg/week) includes your target of −0.35 kg/week. Suggested intake 1,500 kcal/day."
- Maintenance 1,860 ± 330 (Estimated, 44% from my data) — it went DOWN from 1,920/1,970. Target 1,500. Avg intake 1,593, rate −0.23 kg/wk. 6 of last 7 complete?? I ticked every day... (maybe it counts today, which isn't logged yet).
- Protein 93 g vs 125 g. Still low. Body composition still "Not enough data yet".
- Honestly "on track" feels generous when the rate could be +0.08. But I trust it. Plan 1,500.

## Days 23–28 (script)
- Scale 68.5, 68.8, 68.4, 68.6, 69.4, 68.8. Eating 1,370–1,790 (some days over 1,500). Some meals I only had calories for; noticed the protein line says "on 4 logged day(s)" even though all days are complete — I guess it only counts days where every meal had protein. Makes sense once I figured it out.

## Day 29 (Sun 2026-11-01) — got the flu
- Sick. Not weighing, not opening the app, barely eating. Missed the weekly update day too.

## Days 30–38 — sick, app not opened
- Flu. No weigh-ins, no food logged (barely ate: roughly 600–1,100 kcal/day in reality). Missed two Sunday updates (11-01, 11-08).

## Day 39 (Wed 2026-11-11) — back after 10 days
- Scale: 67.6 kg (flu weight...).
- Good news: all my data was still there (the Safari warning had scared me). 28 weigh-ins, 112 food entries, 28 complete days.
- First thing on screen: "It's been 30+ days since your last backup. Back up now / Later." Fair — I'd never backed up. I tapped "Back up now" expecting it to just save a backup; instead it opened a "Your data" page where I had to scroll and tap "Full backup (JSON)". Did that; file saved (downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-11-11.json), "Last backup" now shows 2026-11-11.
- NOTHING acknowledged that I'd been gone for 10 days. No "welcome back", no "you have 10 days with no data — were you sick/travelling?", no offer to tag those days or enter rough totals. The Nutrition tab just shows a column of "not logged" for 11-01…11-10.
- The recommendation box (from the 11-08 update, made while I had logged nothing for a week) still says "On track… Suggested intake 1,510". And the label had switched from "Estimated" to **"Measured" (55% from your data)** — while I wasn't logging anything at all. That felt odd: it became more confident during the week I gave it no data. "0 of the last 7 days complete" right under it.
- Explain the math says missing days are "unknown, not zero" and it assumes the average of my complete days (≈1,600). But I actually ate way less while sick. I worry that when it sees I dropped to 67.6 it will think I burn more than I do. There's no way to tell it "I was sick and barely ate" except to type made-up numbers.
- Weighed 67.6: "▼ 2.6 kg" vs first, trend jumped from 69.1 to 68.1 in one go. Weight chart: the 10-day gap is invisible — points are spaced evenly, so 10-31 → 11-11 looks like one day and the trend line just nosedives at the end. The x labels go 10-22, 10-27, 11-11 at equal spacing. Screenshot: screens/1790459032686.png. Last label "11-11" is also cut off at the right edge.
- Tagged today "Illness" in the Water events (I remembered it from day 1). Only for today — tagging the 10 sick days would mean opening each date one by one.
- Logged 4 meals, 1,550 kcal, complete. Keeping my plan at 1,500.

## Weeks 4 & 5 (days 29, 36) — sick, didn't open the app
- (Seen afterwards: the 11-08 update said On track, maintenance 1,860 ± 300, target 1,510, now "Measured" 55%.)

## Days 40–42 (script)
- Scale 67.8, 67.9, 67.5. Eating 1,390–1,660. Nothing new popped up. The "1 tag" shows next to 11-11 in the 14-day list (my Illness tag).

## Week 6 (update Sun 2026-11-15, day 43)
- Scale 67.0. Trend 67.9. ▼3.2 kg since start.
- App: "On track. Your estimated rate (−0.69 to −0.16 kg/week) includes your target of −0.34 kg/week. Suggested intake: 1,630 kcal/day."
- Maintenance jumped to **1,980 ± 270** (from 1,860), Measured, 63% from my data. Rate −0.43 kg/wk. Protein 92 g vs 122 g.
- Explain the math "cross-check": 2,160 ± 140 kcal/day — a very confident number, but it's drawing a straight line through my flu weeks.
- What I think: the app is telling me to eat MORE (1,630) because my weight dropped during the flu, but it assumed I ate my usual ~1,600 on the days I didn't log. I barely ate. So it now thinks I burn more than I do. The flu kilos will likely come back. Nothing on screen warned me about the gap.
- Decision: NOT following it this week. Staying at 1,500 (plan 1,500).

## Days 44–49 (script)
- Scale 67.0, 66.2, 66.2, 66.5, 66.1, 65.3 — the flu weight did NOT come back, I kept dropping. Eating 1,140–1,880 (avg ~1,500).

## Week 7 (update Sun 2026-11-22, day 50)
- Scale 65.0! ▼5.2 kg since start. Trend 66.9.
- App (first time not "on track"): "Your estimated rate (−0.84 to −0.40 kg/week) doesn't include your target of −0.33 kg/week. Eating about 290 kcal/day more than recently would close the gap. Suggested intake: 1,830 kcal/day."
- Maintenance 2,160 ± 230 (Measured, 73%). Avg intake 1,505, rate −0.62 kg/wk. Protein 88 g vs 120 g.
- So the app's higher maintenance last week was maybe right and I was wrong to doubt it. Still, the maintenance keeps climbing (1,860 → 1,980 → 2,160) and part of that is the flu drop being counted as "normal eating". I can't tell how much.
- Decision: meet it halfway — plan 1,700. I like losing fast, but I'll trust it a bit.

## Days 51–56 (script)
- Scale 65.4, 66.4, 66.1, 66.2, 66.1, 65.3. Eating 1,380–1,940 (a bit over my 1,700 plan sometimes).

## Week 8 (update Sun 2026-11-29, day 57)
- Scale 65.8, trend 66.3, ▼4.4 kg.
- App: "On track. Estimated rate (−0.70 to −0.30 kg/week) includes your target of −0.33. Suggested intake: 1,790 kcal/day."
- Maintenance 2,130 ± 210 (Measured, 77%). Avg intake 1,730. Rate −0.50 kg/wk. Protein 96 g vs 119 g. One macro-mismatch note (11-24, 17% apart).
- Nice to see "On track" again after eating more. Decision: stay around there, plan 1,750.

## Days 58–63 (script)
- Scale 65.9, 66.0, 65.5, 64.7, 65.6, 65.7. Eating 1,150–2,050. Nothing new appeared.

## Week 9 (update Sun 2026-12-06, day 64)
- Scale 65.5, trend 65.9 (▼4.7 kg).
- App: On track (−0.62 to −0.24 kg/wk incl. target −0.33). Suggested 1,790. Maintenance 2,130 ± 200, Measured 79%. Avg 1,636, −0.43 kg/wk. Protein 77 g vs 119 g (worst yet!).
- It always says "6 of last 7 days complete" on Sunday mornings even though I tick every day — today counts before I've eaten. Small thing but it made me double-check my week.
- Decision: no change, stay ~1,750. Need to fix protein.

## Days 65–70 (script)
- Scale 65.5, 66.1, 66.2, 66.2, 65.8, 66.8 — creeping up. Eating 1,340–1,860.
- Day 69 (12-11) the "30+ days since your last backup" banner came back (exactly 30 days after my 11-11 backup). Makes sense.

## Week 10 (update Sun 2026-12-13, day 71)
- Scale 66.8 (▼3.4 kg vs first — was ▼5.2 two weeks ago, sigh).
- App: On track (−0.52 to −0.15 kg/wk incl. −0.33). Suggested 1,680. Maintenance now 2,010 ± 190 (down from 2,130), Measured 81%. Avg 1,644, −0.34 kg/wk. Protein 87 g vs 119 g.
- So the maintenance went 1,860 → 1,980 → 2,160 → 2,130 → 2,130 → 2,010. Looks like the flu bump is washing out. I'd have liked it to not bump up in the first place.
- Backed up again from the banner (downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-12-13.json). Decision: follow it, plan 1,680.

## Days 72–77 (script)
- Scale 66.3, 65.5, 65.5, 65.9, 66.7, 66.2. Eating 1,380–1,930. Nothing new appeared.

## Week 11 (update Sun 2026-12-20, day 78)
- Scale 65.6, trend 66.0 (▼4.6 kg).
- App: On track (−0.55 to −0.15 kg/wk incl. −0.33). Suggested 1,680. Maintenance 2,020 ± 210, Measured 78% (went DOWN from 81% — odd, I logged every day). Avg 1,674, −0.35 kg/wk. Protein 84 vs 119 g.
- Decision: no change, stay at 1,680.

## Days 79–84 (script + last day by hand)
- Scale 65.2, 65.8, 66.2, 65.3, 65.8, 65.7. Eating 1,450–1,850. Day 84: 1,690 kcal, complete. Final trend 65.9 kg (▼4.5 kg vs first, from 70.2).
- A new macro-mismatch note for 12-23 (21% apart).
- Body composition "full breakdown": needs 3 body-fat readings at each end, I have 0. I never entered body fat or tape, so fair enough.
- Weight chart (3M) again: the 10-day flu gap is squeezed to one step; labels 10-15, 10-27, 11-18, 11-30 are equally spaced though they're 12, 22, 12 days apart. Last label "12-26" cut off. screens/1790460253336.png

## End tasks
- ⇩ → "Your data": 74 weigh-ins, 296 food entries, 74 complete days — matches exactly what I did (84 days minus 10 sick days).
- Full backup: downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-12-26.json — opened it; it has all my weights, food, the Illness tag on 11-11, and my settings. Looks complete.
- Daily export (All data, with food entries): downloads/bodytracker-daily_2026-10-04_to_2026-12-26.json — 74 days, one per day, with weight, totals, entries, and "waterTags: illness" on 11-11. The sick days are simply absent (no row saying "no data").
- Also Weights CSV and Food CSV. The weights CSV times are in UTC ("2026-10-05T03:50:00.000Z") even though I weighed at 06:50 my time — would confuse me in a spreadsheet.
- Small thing: on days where one meal had no macros (e.g. 11-15), the daily export has no protein/carbs/fat total at all for that day, even though 3 of 4 meals had them.

## Final review
I liked this app more than I expected. Logging is quick (weigh, four meals, tick "Day complete"), it kept all my data through my 10-day flu break, and the weekly Sunday update stopped me panicking over daily scale jumps. The "On track / eat 290 more" messages were clear and I mostly followed them. Protein reminders were useful, even if I never hit the target.

What bothered me: when I came back after being sick, the app acted like nothing happened. No "welcome back", no question about the missing days — just a backup nag and a list of "not logged". The label had quietly switched to "Measured" while I wasn't logging anything, and the week after I returned it raised my maintenance (1,860 → 1,980 → 2,160) and told me to eat more, apparently because it assumed I ate my normal ~1,600 while I barely ate. I had no way to say "I was sick, I ate much less" short of inventing numbers. The weight chart also hides the gap, so my flu drop looks like a one-day cliff. The "Back up now" button opens a page instead of just backing up, and I had to find the Lose goal in the ⚙ myself after setup.

Would keep using: yes (with an eye on its advice after breaks).
agentReply:
# p10 — Reem (33 F, 158 cm, 70.2 kg start, goal: lose) — final reply

## 1. Usage
- Days I used the app: 74 of 84. Days 1–28 and 39–84; days 29–38 were the flu and I didn't open it.
- Meals logged: 296 (4 a day). Days marked complete: 74. Weigh-ins: 74 (the profile weight counted as day 1's).
- Weight went from 70.2 to 65.7 kg (trend 65.9, ▼4.5 kg). The app's data screen showed exactly these counts.

## 2. Weekly table
| week (update day) | maintenance shown | target | label | recommendation | what I did |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| start d1 10-04 | 1,870 ± 440 | 1,510 (after I picked Lose) | Estimated 0% | on-track check needs 14 days | picked Lose 0.5%/wk |
| W1 d8 10-11 | 1,970 ± 430 | 1,620 | Estimated 4% | suggested 1,620; check needs 14 days | plan 1,620 |
| W2 d15 10-18 | 1,920 ± 390 | 1,570 | Estimated 22% | On track (−0.73…+0.02 incl. −0.35) | plan 1,570 |
| W3 d22 10-25 | 1,860 ± 330 | 1,500 | Estimated 44% | On track (−0.55…+0.08) | plan 1,500 |
| W4 d29 11-01 | — (sick, not opened) | — | — | — | nothing |
| W5 d36 11-08 (seen d39) | 1,860 ± 300 | 1,510 | **Measured 55%** (no data that week) | On track (−0.58…+0.02) | kept 1,500 |
| W6 d43 11-15 | 1,980 ± 270 | 1,630 | Measured 63% | On track, eat 1,630 | ignored it; I thought the flu loss was inflating it; stayed at 1,500 |
| W7 d50 11-22 | 2,160 ± 230 | 1,830 | Measured 73% | Losing too fast (−0.84…−0.40); eat +290 | half-followed: plan 1,700 |
| W8 d57 11-29 | 2,130 ± 210 | 1,790 | Measured 77% | On track | plan 1,750 |
| W9 d64 12-06 | 2,130 ± 200 | 1,790 | Measured 79% | On track | no change |
| W10 d71 12-13 | 2,010 ± 190 | 1,680 | Measured 81% | On track | plan 1,680 |
| W11 d78 12-20 | 2,020 ± 210 | 1,680 | Measured 78% | On track | no change |

## 3. Confusions
- Setup: there was no goal question, so the target read "maintain" until I found Lose under ⚙ on the Nutrition tab.
- Body tab: tapping the big "Weight" tile opens a chart. You have to use the small "+ Weight" button to log.
- Recommendation: "needs 14 days of data (day 1 so far)" stayed the same all through week 1. I only understood it was frozen at the weekly update after I read Explain the math.
- The "Day complete" tick sits above the add-entry form, so I nearly missed it.
- Protein average: "on 4 logged day(s)" appeared while all 7 days were complete. Days with any meal missing protein are dropped silently.
- On Sunday mornings it always showed "6 of last 7 days complete", because today counts before I've eaten.
- Return after the flu: nothing mentioned the 10-day gap. There was no welcome back, and no prompt to mark or roughly fill the missing days. The only way to tag Illness was one date at a time.
- The label switched from Estimated to Measured (44% → 55%) during a week with zero data.
- "Back up now" opens the "Your data" page. It doesn't back up; you still have to scroll and tap "Full backup (JSON)".
- The macro mismatch notes (16–21% apart) came from my own label numbers. I didn't know which figure to fix, so I left them.
- Data share fell from 81% to 78% while I was logging every day.

## 4. Possible bugs / issues
1. **Flu gap pushes maintenance up.** Steps: log normally about 1,600 kcal/day for 4 weeks, then log nothing and eat very little for 10 days, then come back and weigh 1.2 kg lighter. Expected: the app says the unlogged days are uncertain, or asks about them, and doesn't read the drop as higher burn. Actual: maintenance went 1,860 → 1,980 (d43) → 2,160 (d50) and the suggested intake rose to 1,630, then 1,830. Explain the math's cross-check showed "2,160 ± 140" from a straight-line fit through the gap. It settled back to about 2,010 by d71. Screens: screens/1790459161413.png, screens/1790459355760.png.
2. **Weight chart hides time gaps.** The x-axis spaces points by entry, not by date. The 11-day gap from 10-31 to 11-11 takes one step, labels 12 or 22 days apart are equally spaced, and the trend line shows a one-day cliff. The last date label is also clipped at the right edge. Screens: screens/1790459032686.png, screens/1790460253336.png.
3. **Became "Measured" with no data.** The 11-08 update came during a week with 0 of 7 days logged and no weigh-ins. It moved the label to Measured (55%) and still said "On track". Screen: screens/1790459001742.png.
4. **Backup banner button.** "Back up now" opens the data page and doesn't create a backup. Expected a one-tap backup. Screen: after screens/1790458982944.png.
5. Minor: the Weights CSV gives times in UTC (03:50Z for a 06:50 local weigh-in). The daily export leaves out that day's protein, carbs and fat totals whenever any one meal lacks macros (e.g. 11-15).

## 5. Review
Logging was quick, my data survived the 10 days away, and the Sunday "On track / eat X more" messages kept me calm about daily scale swings. I lost about 4.5 kg. Coming back after being sick felt like the app hadn't noticed I was gone. It quietly assumed I'd eaten normally, called its estimate "Measured", and then told me to eat more for two weeks. The chart made my flu drop look like a one-day crash. I'd like a "you were away. Anything unusual?" moment.

Would keep using: **yes**.
